subject: RFI: Phased activation questionnaire + rollback and acceptance criteria — CrescentBank

Subject: RFI: phased activation requirements + questions about rollback windows

Hi Priyom / Marissa,

Thanks for the prior materials — the Security & Ops teams at Crescent have one focused area of follow-up before we enter procurement: we need a clear phased-activation questionnaire that calls out the following for each activation phase:

- Exact integration touchpoints (API endpoints, event consumers)
- Pre-cutover smoke tests and success gates (SLOs we can validate)
- Canary sizing and duration for traffic ramp
- Observability and telemetry requirements (traces, token-level cost logs)
- Rollback/backout triggers and maximum mitigation window

Can you provide a short form response and a sample runbook excerpt that ties the above to a 3-phase migration (pilot -> regional ramp -> global)?

We expect to review this with our Cloud Ops on Monday morning (PST). If you can include who would be on-call from Redwood during each phase that would help our scheduling.

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Re: RFI: phased activation requirements + questions about rollback windows

Alex —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached is a compact questionnaire matrix (crescent_integration_matrix.xlsx) plus a short runbook excerpt (PDF) that maps a 3-phase activation to acceptance gates. High level here: 

Phase 0 (Pilot, single app/team) — 24-72 hours:
- Integration points: one write path (POST /generate), one read path (GET /status) 
- Smoke tests: end-to-end generation sample through dev dataset; 99th %ile latency < 500ms on 95% of requests; error rate < 0.5% for 24h
- Canary: 1% of traffic directed via feature-flagged router for 48 hours
- Telemetry: token-level cost logs, request id tracing, prefix/KV-cache hit-rate metrics
- Rollback triggers: sustained error rate > 1% for 30 minutes OR latency 95p > 700ms for 30 minutes
- DRI: Engineering on-call + Solutions contact (listed in the runbook)

Phase 1 (Region ramp) — 3–7 days:
- Integration points: all region-specific endpoints, cross-region failover validated
- Smoke tests: sample production traffic replay at 10% of normal volume; A/B quality checks against baseline prompts
- Canary: 10% traffic for 72 hours with step-up increments after each 24h validation window
- Telemetry: additionally enable span-level logs for trace sampling at 5%
- Rollback triggers: same as Phase 0 but thresholds tightened with automated fallback to previous model variant

Phase 2 (Global activation) — gated with automated fallback:
- Integration points: full topology enabled, autoscaling policies at expected trough/peak levels
- Smoke tests: full traffic cutover during a maintenance window with blue/green routing available
- Canary: progressive step from 25% -> 50% -> 100% over a 48–72h window, each step gated by automated validation
- Rollback: immediate rollback if any critical data path error or regression in quality metrics (see runbook thresholds)

I've put the on-call roster and contact SLAs in the runbook. If you want, we can swap the 10%/25% canary sizing depending on your traffic profile.

I attached the two files inline and pasted the most relevant acceptance metrics above to speed review. Happy to hop on a 30-min call Monday 09:00 PST to walk through.

Best,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI: phased activation requirements + questions about rollback windows

Marissa / team — quick technical confirmations and additions:

1) KV cache scoping: yes — cache namespace can be tenant-scoped. Warm-up: we recommend pre-warming by replaying the top-1000 active prefixes for 2 hours before Phase 1 ramp; this is documented in the attached matrix.

2) Gating automation: we can ship a validation pipeline that executes smoke tests and computes acceptance metrics (latency percentiles, error-rate, token-cost delta). The pipeline exposes a webhook that Crescent can use to block router progress unless acceptance=true.

3) Telemetry retention & audit: default production retention is 90 days for traces and 365 days for aggregated cost/usage by token cohort; we can provide 365 days for traces on an enterprise contract addendum.

4) Rollback automation: we support immediate model variant fallback and route-level traffic split rollback. For full-backout we recommend a 2-stage backout: immediate route split to previous variant (automated) + full rollback to previous model image (manual approval after incident review).

5) Canary sizing suggestion: for high-risk endpoints we should prefer smaller initial ramps (0.5% -> 2% -> 10%) with a minimum observation window of 24h per step. For lower-risk read-only endpoints the 1% -> 10% cadence is OK.

I'll update the runbook with the warm-up instructions and webhook payload examples.

Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer — Redwood Inference
